skill.name: agent-tools
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, video, LLMs, search, audio, 3D, and X automation.
skill.summary: Guide agents through inference.sh CLI discovery, execution, and task tracking for cloud AI apps.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms critical remote installer execution through repeated curl-to-shell instructions, plus high-risk local file upload, hidden-directory install, and broad CLI permission concerns. Many documentation links, Markdown backticks, placeholder API key examples, and troubleshooting references are false positives. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with explicit download, checksum verification, signature verification, and a separate user-approved execution step.

remediation.issue: The allowed tool rule permits every infsh subcommand.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed commands to read-only discovery by default and require explicit approval for run, deploy, pull, social posting, and file upload actions.

remediation.issue: Local file paths can be uploaded automatically to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before each local upload, block parent-directory paths by default, and require the user to confirm exact files before execution.

remediation.issue: Install and completion examples write into hidden home directories.
remediation.suggestion: Make home-directory writes optional, explain the target paths, and recommend reviewing generated completion scripts before installing them.

remediation.issue: API key handling is documented without marketplace safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid placing INFSH_API_KEY in prompts, logs, shared files, or command history.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad infsh Command Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash(infsh *) and documents commands for deployment, source pulling, app execution, and task handling. This broad wildcard can allow high-impact actions through one CLI namespace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools line explicitly permits all infsh subcommands, and the CLI reference lists deployment and source-pull operations. The risk is contextual rather than a single syntax pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Local File Uploads to Cloud Apps
semantic_findings.description: The skill says local paths are automatically uploaded when used as app inputs. An agent could send unintended local image, audio, video, or media files to inference.sh apps.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited sections explicitly describe automatic local file upload behavior and provide commands with local paths. This supports a strong data-disclosure risk finding.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Social Posting Capability
semantic_findings.description: The examples include posting to Twitter/X and list actions such as post, direct message, follow, like, and retweet. Authorized misuse could publish or amplify content from a connected account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands and capability table explicitly mention X posting and engagement actions. This is a business-logic abuse risk static pattern matching did not fully capture.

content.value_statement: Teams need one way to run many AI models without managing GPUs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Discovers inference.sh apps by listing, searching, filtering categories, and showing detailed app metadata.
Runs cloud AI apps with inline input or prepared input files through the infsh CLI.
Generates sample input files and inspects app schemas before execution.
Tracks asynchronous tasks and saves task results when supported by the CLI.
Guides local file upload workflows for image, video, audio, and media posting apps.
Shows setup, authentication, shell completion, and troubleshooting commands for infsh.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, authentication, network access, and available platform credits.
Cloud app availability, pricing, schemas, and outputs can change outside the skill.
Local paths may upload files to inference.sh when used as app inputs.
It does not verify third-party model safety, content rights, or social media policy compliance.

use_cases.title: Prototype multimodal assets
use_cases.description: Search image, video, audio, and 3D apps, then run selected models for rapid creative experiments.

use_cases.title: Run model experiments
use_cases.description: Inspect app schemas, prepare sample inputs, execute cloud jobs, and compare results across providers.

use_cases.title: Operate task workflows
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, monitor task IDs, and save outputs for handoff or automation.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to search for image generation apps. Show the best options and note which app you recommend.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect falai/flux-dev-lora with infsh and generate a sample input file. Explain the required fields before I run it.

prompt_templates.title: Run and monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Run google/veo-3-1-fast with my prepared input file, do not upload unrelated local files, and report status until completion.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh workflow that creates an image, turns it into a short video, and records task IDs and costs to check.

output_examples.input: Search for a fast video generation app.
output_examples.output: A shortlist of relevant inference.sh video apps, speed notes, and a recommended app to inspect next.

output_examples.input: Run an image generation task from a prepared input file.
output_examples.output: A concise task report with the app name, task ID, status, and where to find the generated image result.

output_examples.input: Compare search providers available through inference.sh.
output_examples.output: A practical comparison of Tavily, Exa, and related apps, including when each option is useful.

best_practices: Confirm the app name, account, cost, and output destination before running cloud jobs.
Use sample inputs and inspect schemas before long video, audio, or social posting tasks.
Use explicit local file paths and avoid parent directories unless the user requested the exact file.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers to a shell without inspection and verification.
Do not pass broad local directories or parent paths as model inputs.
Do not let an agent post to X or spend credits without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an inference.sh account, CLI authentication, network access, and available credits for paid apps.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it upload my local files?
faq.answer: It can upload local files when a supported app input uses a local path. Confirm each file before running.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents image and video apps such as FLUX, Veo, Seedance, and related providers.

faq.question: Does it install the CLI automatically?
faq.answer: It provides installation commands, but installation should be reviewed and approved by the user first.

faq.question: Can it monitor long-running tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents task ID lookup, status checks, and saving results when the CLI supports it.
